description:
RULED s338 (fable-answers-s337.md §5a). PCL tracks no warnings state anywhere (grepped Pl/ and cl/, s337c). Consequence: every perl diagnostic must be unconditional or absent, and unconditional is WRONG for anything default-off (measured s337c: "print() on unopened filehandle" is use-warnings-gated; emitting it broke fileio-02.t + transpile-test-09.t).

NOT a non-goal — CPAN compatibility eventually needs warnings-gated diagnostics (Test::Warnings, Carp behaviors, the print warning above). But nothing schedules it today.

Minimal viable shape (v1): `use warnings`/`no warnings` compiled per lexical scope into a dynamic var the runtime consults; ONE boolean, no categories. Category granularity only when a concrete consumer demands it.

TRIGGER to schedule: the first test family or CPAN module whose failure is "warning not emitted / emitted when off". Until then the standing rule holds: default-off diagnostics are ABSENT, never unconditional.

TRIGGER FIRED s399 (#323): assignwarn.t 20 + hashassign.t 4 sweep rows,
op/numify.t 11 + op/utf8decode.t 86 companion rows â 145 rows, ONE cause
(no warnings-gated diagnostic).  RULED s401 (docs/fable-answers-s400.md Â§4):
status UNSCHEDULED -> SCHEDULED as the FIRST item of the post-v0.1
correctness backlog, NOT in the v0.1 track.  Design constraint: ZERO cost on
the non-undef path â the "Use of uninitialized value" check may live only on
the branch that already knows the value is undef (to-string/to-number undef
arm); needs the bench (R2 instrument).  v1 shape unchanged: ONE lexical
boolean compiled from `use warnings`/`no warnings` per scope into a dynamic
var; only diagnostics with a MEASURED consumer (uninitialized value;
odd-elements hash assign; print on unopened handle).  Standing rule until
then: default-off diagnostics stay ABSENT, never unconditional.
subject: Design: minimal `use warnings` model (lexical boolean, no categories) — UNSCHEDULED until a concrete consumer
